blocks.text: Proxys.io in 2026: what you get

Proxys.io is a per-IP proxy shop rather than a bandwidth network. Its catalog covers shared IPv4 (up to three users per IP), dedicated IPv4, cheap IPv6 from $0.13 per address, premium residential IPv4, rotating residential packages and SIM-based mobile proxies. You rent each IP for days or months, bandwidth is generally unlimited on dedicated IPs, and a 24-hour refund window replaces a trial. It is popular with affiliate marketers and multi-account operators who want fixed addresses rather than a rotating pool.

Strengths: Low-entry per-address products; a provider-reported 100M+ residential network; country, region and city targeting; HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS5 included; a 24-hour refund window. Weak spots: Rotating mobile traffic pricing must be checked in the cart; residential plans have 30/60/90-day validity; published pool totals do not guarantee reachable IPs; independent target-specific performance has not been established here.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap has sold proxies since 2018 and says it serves 45,000+ customers. It offers seven product types: static residential (ISP) in IPv4 and IPv6, rotating residential, datacenter IPv4 and IPv6, and static and rotating mobile. Rotating residential is pure pay-as-you-go with no monthly plan, and the site claims coverage in 180+ countries. Targeting is mainly country and ISP level, and all products support SOCKS5 including UDP. It is a strong value pick, though independent benchmarks of its rotating pool have been mixed.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: Proxys.io vs Proxy-Cheap

PROXYS.IO separates traffic-based plans from per-address rentals. Rotating residential starts at $1.50/GB on 30, 60 or 90-day plans, without an IP or session cap. Static monthly starting prices are IPv6 $0.13, dynamic $0.27, shared IPv4 $0.67 (up to three users), foreign individual IPv4 $1.47, Windows-fingerprint IPv4 $1.87 and premium static residential IPv4 $3.60. Dedicated mobile IPv4 with unlimited traffic on a private channel starts at $56.79/month. Rotating mobile traffic is priced by the cart slider; no single starting per-GB rate has been confirmed. HEAT_RES provides 35% off eligible residential pay-per-traffic plans. Minimum static rental is one month and the refund window is 24 hours.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

At 10 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; Proxy-Cheap comes to about $7.80. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Proxys.io does not publish an exact price for that volume; Proxy-Cheap comes to about $78. Both Proxys.io and Proxy-Cheap work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxys.io and Proxy-Cheap do not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. Proxys.io reports 100M+ addresses and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, Proxys.io lists 195 residential countries, with separate mobile and static coverage countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, Proxys.io offers country, region and city for residential traffic, with city/carrier selection for mobile, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Proxys.io offers static per-IP proxies; rotating residential and mobile, and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: compare the exact target and traffic plan before choosing. PROXYS.IO reports a 100M+ rotating residential network across 195 countries, in addition to static rentals. Pool size alone does not establish success rate; this brief does not independently benchmark PROXYS.IO against the other provider.

SERP and rank tracking: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Proxys.io: cheap IPv6 can handle some search tasks. With Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Social media and multi-account management: Proxys.io wins. The deciding factor for Proxys.io: fixed dedicated or mobile IPs per account. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: fine for country-level price checks. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: limited rotation for large catalog crawls.

Ad verification and geo-testing: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Proxys.io: limited geo depth. With Proxy-Cheap: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the Proxys.io side: cheap per-IP rentals with unlimited bandwidth.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. Proxys.io: Light; crypto accepted. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Proxys.io and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Proxys.io vs Proxy-Cheap faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Proxys.io: 24-hour refund window instead of a trial; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Proxys.io comes out ahead in 1, Proxy-Cheap in 3, and 2 are ties. That makes Proxy-Cheap the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Proxys.io is strongest for multi-account and affiliate work that needs fixed IPs, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
